newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-FRENCH NO BETTER THAN ENGLAND, CLAIMS ROWELL.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-FRENCH NO BETTER THAN ENGLAND, CLAIMS ROWELL.

text.p: England coach Jack Rowell claimed on Saturday there was little to choose between his side and France after watching the Five Nations title slip away.

Rowell conceded England had blown their grand slam chances when they threw away a 20-6 lead at Twickenham two weeks ago but hailed the record 34-13 win over Wales in Cardiff as proof his team had made significant progress during the season.
"I think we've taken big steps forward this year," said Rowell after England registered only their third win in Cardiff in more than 30 years.

"We learnt a lesson from the French experience....a lesser team might have thought it was not worth bothering. I know France have won the title and Brive won the European Cup but I don't see anything between French and English rugby that justifies them winning as they have at international and club level."
Rowell also indicated he felt the gap between England and the best southern hemisphere sides was closing.
"We're playing Australia, New Zealand and South Africa at home next season and provided the top players don't play too much and lose their edge, I think England are on the up," he said.
Several England players cemented places on the Lions tour to South Africa, but Welsh fly-half Neil Jenkins looks almost certain to miss out.
Welsh coach Kevin Bowring indicated the full-back might have to have a plate inserted to mend the broken arm he suffered inside the first 15 minutes against England.
Welsh captain Jonathan Humphreys nevertheless refused to blame a long list of injuries for his side's big loss against what he felt was a much-improved England side,
Two members of the English pack -- Mark Regan and Simon Shaw -- were also taken to hospital for X-rays on ankle injuries and Rowell said it had been a hectic day on the replacements' bench.
"There were all kinds of people running on at the end. I couldn't stop them," he laughed. The most popular arrival was Rob Andrew, who replaced Mike Catt with eight minutes left.
